ours.name: BettaTool (HRNet-W32 + probabilistic heads, v3)
ours.training: 1,161 training images (70%), ImageNet-pretrained backbone, fish-box crop input

mfld.name: MFLD-Net (retrained)
mfld.training: 1,127 training images (68%) from scratch, fish-box crop input, same split

protocol: Both models scored against our annotations on the same 247 held-out test images, in original-photo pixels, with the labelled fish box as the crop. Error figures are lower-is-better; PCK and accuracy are higher-is-better.

rows.label: Test images where the model has the lower mean keypoint error
Measurement error, 5 IBC criteria (relative)
rows.note: Each criterion is scored on every test image where its own keypoints are labelled: caudal-spread-angle 247, dorsal-body-ratio 247, anal-body-ratio 247, caudal-body-ratio 242, anal-length-width-ratio 247 images.

rows.label: Pass/Fault accuracy, 5 criteria
rows.note: BettaTool without deferral and MFLD-Net both answer every case. BettaTool with deferral answers only the cases its uncertainty says it can decide, so its accuracy is over those cases only. Reference: always answering each criterion's most common outcome, with no model at all, scores 94.7% (the test set is mostly Pass / mostly Fault per criterion).

rows.label: Share of cases the system gives an answer on
rows.note: The rest are deferred to a human judge by BettaTool's gate. MFLD-Net has no deferral, so it answers every case.

examples_note: 8 test images drawn at random (fixed seeds), not hand-picked. Green = human label, blue = BettaTool, orange = MFLD-Net.
caveats: MFLD-Net is far smaller and faster; the accuracy gap partly reflects model size and ImageNet pretraining.
The live overlay in the app feeds both models the whole photo (the app has no fish detector), which is harder than the benchmark input.
A single uploaded photo has no ground truth, so differences on one image show disagreement, not which model is right.
